$comment: Sealed golden bundles. See README.md before touching anything in this directory.

goldens.why: The smallest conformant bundle: the hand-written example the validator was first written against, independent of the exporter. Catches any change that makes a bare-bones bundle unreadable.
goldens.roleReason: Hand-written against the spec in Phase 0 and NEVER produced by Charcoal's exporter. Tier 2 found it carries company.Code — a column that has never existed on the Company entity — so it cannot be imported and never could have been. It stays as a VALIDATOR-conformance golden (the minimal shape a reader must accept); it is not evidence about the importer, and the 36-month promise covers bundles PRODUCED BY CHARCOAL, which this is not.

goldens.why: A real exporter's output across 8 module databases, carrying the shapes a minimal bundle never exercises: embedded children, numbering watermarks, the resolved-settings sidecar, per-DB snapshot consistency, pseudonymized values.
goldens.provenance: backends examples/acme-mini (the Phase-4 committed fixture, produced by the real exporter)
goldens.roleReason: Real exporter output: the golden that carries the import promise.

goldens.why: A bundle produced by a third party rather than by Charcoal — the migration profile, with the allocate id-policy hint, $source provenance on every record and control totals. This is the golden that proves the format is writable from outside, which is the whole no-lock-in claim.
goldens.roleReason: allocate-mode: organization and company are ANCHORS resolved by natural key on the target, so this bundle REQUIRES the tenant to already exist. Tier 2 imports 1.0-full first and layers this on top without truncating in between — which is also exactly how a real adapter migration runs.

$roles.conformance: Tier 1 only — must verify and keep its pinned digest. Not imported, and NOT field-checked against the current entity manifest.
$roles.importer: Tier 1 (verify + digest + resourceVersion + FIELD compatibility against the current entity manifest) and tier 2 (actually restored into a stack).
